**A is better.** Response A comes in at roughly 119–121 words, depending on whether the list numerals count, so it is at or just under the 120-word limit. Response B runs to about 134 words and clearly exceeds it.

On content, both explain chaining, open addressing, load factor, average O(1) versus worst-case O(n), and resizing. B adds the Java HashMap tree detail and a concrete load-factor threshold. A adds the amortized O(1) cost of resizing, which directly answers the performance question.

Since the content is comparable and A respects the length constraint while B breaks it, A wins.
